newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open weaker, interest in property.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open weaker, interest in property.

text.p: Singapore shares opened weaker on Tuesday but could be in the mood for an upturn as attention turned to a potential deal in the property sector, dealers said.
"All the action will be in property today," one dealer with a local institution said.
At 0430 GMT the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 5.70 points at 2,055.20.
The suspension of DBS Land shares ahead of an expected placement of 92 million shares raised speculation that the firm would raise its stake in healthcare group Parkway Holdings.
DBS Land has said it might raise its 19.2 percent stake.
"Some of the land that Parkway hospitals are on are prime development sites and I think that's an angle few people have looked at before now," one dealer said.
But the Stock Exchange of Singapore Property index was almost unchanged by the news, off 0.67 at 709.96 at 0240 GMT.
Marketwide, activity was muted with 49.2 million shares traded by 0240 GMT to give 90 gainers and 83 losers.
Most active was new listing Benefun International with 9.5 million shares traded to see it stand at Hong Kong $1.55 against an offer price of HK$1.15.
